You have a Microsoft 365 subscription synchronized with Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS).  
  
You must define recovery steps for a ransomware attack that encrypted data in the subscription. The solution must comply with Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
What should be the first step in the recovery plan?

options.text: From Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, perform a security scan.
Recover files to a cleaned computer or device.
Disable Microsoft OneDrive sync and Exchange ActiveSync.

questions.explanation:
Ransomware response begins with containment. Disabling OneDrive sync prevents potentially infected devices from updating cloud data, and disabling Exchange ActiveSync stops mobile synchronization. Microsoft’s ransomware playbook lists this action under preventing the attack from spreading, before malware removal, security scanning, and file recovery.

**Learn more:** [Responding to ransomware attacks - Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/playbook-responding-ransomware-m365-defender)

questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing several storage accounts. Legacy applications access the storage accounts by authenticating with access keys.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that prevents new applications from obtaining the storage-account access keys. The solution must minimize the effect on the legacy applications.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Set the AllowSharedKeyAccess property to false.
Apply read-only locks on the storage accounts.
Set the AllowBlobPublicAccess property to false.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Resource Manager ReadOnly lock blocks the storage account List Keys operation, which returns the account access keys. Applications that already possess access keys can continue to use them for data access, minimizing impact on legacy key-authenticated applications. [Lock resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources)

**Learn more:** [Lock resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources) · [Apply an Azure Resource Manager lock to a storage account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/lock-account-resource)

questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are defining security standards for containerized applications being onboarded to Azure.  
  
You are assessing the use of Microsoft Defender for Containers.  
  
In which two environments can Defender for Containers scan for known vulnerabilities? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Linux containers deployed to Azure Container Instances
Windows containers deployed to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
Windows containers deployed to Azure Container Registry
Linux containers deployed to Azure Container Registry
Linux containers deployed to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

questions.explanation:
Defender for Containers performs container-registry vulnerability assessment for images in Azure Container Registry (ACR), and the supported operating systems include Linux distributions and Windows Server container images. Thus, both Linux and Windows container images stored in ACR can be scanned for known vulnerabilities.

**Learn more:** [Containers support matrix in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/support-matrix-defender-for-containers) · [Overview of Microsoft Defender for Containers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-containers-introduction)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend access restrictions that allow traffic from the backend IP address of the Front Door instance.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door origin traffic uses a changing set of IP ranges represented by the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag, rather than one backend IP address. Restricting an App Service to a specific Front Door instance also requires filtering the `X-Azure-FDID` header for that instance’s identifier.\
\
**Learn more:** [App Service access restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-access-restrictions) · [Secure traffic to Azure Front Door origins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/origin-security)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend access restrictions that permit traffic from the Front Door service tags.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag permits traffic from the backend IP ranges used by all Azure Front Door instances, not only a particular instance. Restricting an App Service origin to a specific Azure Front Door instance also requires filtering the unique `X-Azure-FDID` header that Front Door sends.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure App Service access restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-access-restrictions) · [Secure traffic to Azure Front Door origins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/origin-security)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend access restrictions that are based on HTTP headers containing the Front Door ID.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An App Service access restriction based only on the `X-Azure-FDID` header can be bypassed by a direct request that supplies the same header. Restricting access to a particular Azure Front Door instance requires both an allow rule for the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag and an `X-Azure-FDID` header restriction.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set Up Access Restrictions - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-ip-restrictions)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: Recommend access restrictions that permit traffic from the Front Door service tags.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure App Service access restrictions can use the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag to allow traffic originating from Azure Front Door and block other inbound public traffic. Filtering additionally on `X-Azure-FDID` is required only when access must be limited to a specific Front Door instance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure App Service access restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-access-restrictions) · [Create a multi-region app with Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/tutorial-multi-region-app)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend configuring gateway-required virtual network integration.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Gateway-required virtual network integration provides outbound connectivity from an Azure App Service app to resources in a virtual network. It does not provide private inbound access or restrict the app’s public endpoint to Azure Front Door traffic, so it cannot ensure that the web apps are accessible only through the Front Door instance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration) · [Configure gateway-required virtual network integration for your app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-gateway-required-vnet-integration)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend access restrictions that are based on HTTP headers containing the Front Door ID.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
App Service HTTP-header filters are evaluated only in addition to the access-restriction rule’s source condition. To ensure that an app is reached only through a specific Azure Front Door instance, allow the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag and require the matching `X-Azure-FDID` header; a header-only restriction does not prevent direct spoofed requests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up access restrictions - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-ip-restrictions) · [Secure traffic to origins - Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/origin-security)

The company wants to identify and classify data in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, and Exchange Online.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for identifying documents that contain sensitive information.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

It can be used to drill into Exchange, Teams, and SharePoint locations to locate the classified content. [Get started with Content Explorer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/purview/data-classification-content-explorer)\

questions.question:
Your company has a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
The company wants to identify and classify data in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, and Exchange Online.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for identifying documents that contain sensitive information.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: app discovery anomaly detection policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Azure Security Benchmark compliance controls in Defender for Cloud
application control policies in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

questions.explanation:
Application control policies enforce an allowlist of trusted code on Windows Server 2019, preventing unapproved applications and installers from executing until they meet an authorized rule. Microsoft documents App Control for Business (WDAC) as restricting which applications and code can run, including support for Windows Server 2019.

**Learn more:** [WDAC enforced infrastructure in Windows Admin Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/manage/windows-admin-center/use/manage-application-control-infrastructure) · [App Control for Business feature availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/feature-availability)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription with enhanced security enabled in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
The company signs a contract with the United States government.  
  
You need to review the current subscription for compliance with NIST 800-53.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Defender for Cloud, review the secure score recommendations.
From Microsoft Sentinel, configure the Microsoft Defender for Cloud data connector.
From Defender for Cloud, review the Azure security baseline for audit report.
From Defender for Cloud, add a regulatory compliance standard.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud evaluates a subscription against a regulatory framework only after that framework is assigned as a regulatory compliance standard. NIST SP 800-53 is available as a standard but is not enabled by default for Azure subscriptions; enabling it allows the Regulatory compliance dashboard to assess in-scope resources and report compliance status and remediation recommendations.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains 100 virtual machines running Windows Server. The virtual machines are managed by using Azure Policy and Microsoft Defender for Servers.  
  
You need to improve security on the virtual machines. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that only applications on an allowlist can run.  
- Require administrators to confirm every app added to the allowlist.  
- Automatically place unauthorized apps on a blocklist when an attempt is made to launch an app.  
- Require administrator approval before an app can be moved from the blocklist to the allowlist.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: a compute policy in Azure Policy
app governance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
admin consent settings for enterprise applications in Microsoft Entra ID
adaptive application controls in Defender for Servers

questions.explanation:
Adaptive application controls in Defender for Servers provide VM application control by learning known-safe applications, generating allowlist rules, and detecting applications outside those rules for administrative review and enforcement. This directly addresses executable application allowlisting and the controlled handling of unapproved applications on Windows Server VMs. Microsoft now lists Adaptive application controls as deprecated, but it is the capability described by this exam item.

**Learn more:** [Reference table for compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud release notes archive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/release-notes-archive)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You also have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy a Microsoft Purview communication compliance solution for Microsoft Teams and Yammer. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Assign compliance policies to Microsoft 365 groups based on custom Microsoft Exchange Online attributes.  
- Minimize the number of compliance policies.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
Adaptive scopes use dynamic queries to define the Microsoft 365 groups targeted by compliance policies. They support Exchange custom attributes and can be used with Communication Compliance policies; a single policy can include one or more adaptive scopes, which reduces policy count and ongoing manual administration.

**Learn more:** [Adaptive scopes | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes) · [Create and manage Communication Compliance policies | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/communication-compliance-policies)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer uses Azure to develop a mobile app that external users will consume, as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809593706-xxek3fwy.jpg)  
  
You need to design an identity strategy for the app. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Enable the use of external IDs such as Google, Facebook, and Microsoft accounts.  
- Use a customer identity store.  
- Support fully customizable branding for the app.  
  
Which service should you recommend to complete the design?

options.text: Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS)

questions.explanation:
Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) B2C supports customer identities stored in a B2C tenant and federation with social identity providers including Google, Facebook, and Microsoft accounts. Its user flows and custom policies provide customizable sign-in and other identity experiences to match an application's branding.

**Learn more:** [Add an identity provider to your Azure Active Directory B2C tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/add-identity-provider) · [Technical and feature overview - Azure Active Directory B2C](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/technical-overview)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Defender portal, you turn on Web content filtering and create a web content filtering policy.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Web content filtering controls access to websites by content category, not by Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps risk scores for SaaS applications. Cloud app risk scores and policies that identify and govern high-risk apps are required to allow low-risk SaaS apps while blocking high-risk SaaS apps.\
\
**Learn more:** [Web content filtering - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/web-content-filtering) · [Cloud app catalog and risk scores - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/risk-score)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: Configure app protection policies in Intune and create a Conditional Access policy.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Intune app protection policies protect organizational data within supported managed applications, and Conditional Access can restrict access to organizational resources through approved or protected client apps. They do not provide risk-score-based allow/block control for SaaS apps discovered and rated by Microsoft. Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps discovery and governance capabilities are required to identify risky SaaS apps and block unsanctioned apps.\
\
**Learn more:** [App Protection Policies Overview - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/protection/overview) · [Govern discovered apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/governance-discovery)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: In Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, configure a cloud discovery policy and unsanction risky apps.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Cloud Discovery policy can detect apps according to their risk score and tag matching high-risk apps as Unsanctioned. With Defender for Endpoint integration, Unsanctioned apps are synchronized for blocking, while low-risk apps that are not tagged remain available.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud discovery policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-cloud-discovery) · [Govern discovered apps using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/mde-govern)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
Solution: In Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, configure a cloud discovery policy and unsanction risky apps.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
SSPM provides security-posture visibility for supported connected SaaS apps, while access policies control sign-ins to apps in the Conditional Access App Control scope. They do not govern general user access to discovered SaaS apps according to Microsoft’s cloud-app risk ratings. Defender for Cloud Apps evaluates discovered apps using its risk indicators; high-risk apps can be marked **Unsanctioned** and, with the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration, blocked through network protection. [Cloud app catalog and risk scores](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/risk-score), [Govern discovered apps using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/mde-govern)

**Learn more:** [Cloud app catalog and risk scores](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/risk-score) · [Govern discovered apps using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/mde-govern)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and an Azure subscription. Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are enabled.  
  
The Azure subscription includes 50 virtual machines. Every virtual machine runs distinct applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be automatically blocked until an administrator authorizes it.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

options.text: app registrations in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
OAuth app policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Azure Security Benchmark compliance controls in Defender for Cloud
application control policies in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

questions.explanation:
Application control policies in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint use Windows application-control capabilities to enforce an allowlist of trusted applications and code on Windows Server 2019. They can prevent unauthorized executables, scripts, and installers from running until an administrator updates the policy to authorize them.

**Learn more:** [WDAC enforced infrastructure in Windows Admin Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/manage/windows-admin-center/use/manage-application-control-infrastructure) · [App Control for Business operational guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/operations/appcontrol-operational-guide)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities

options.text: From Azure Policy, assign a built-in initiative that has a scope of the subscription.
From Microsoft Sentinel, configure the Microsoft Defender for Cloud data connector.
From Defender for Cloud, review the Azure security baseline for audit report.
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, create an access policy for cloud applications.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud implements regulatory compliance standards through Azure Policy initiatives and evaluates them for the assigned scope. Assigning the built-in NIST 800-53 initiative to the subscription enables the compliance assessment needed to review that subscription.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are defining security standards for a new Azure environment.  
  
You need to create a privileged-identity strategy founded on the Zero Trust model.  
  
Which framework should you use to develop the design?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft’s modern privileged-access strategy is built on Zero Trust principles, including explicit validation, least privilege, and assuming breach. Microsoft identifies Rapid Modernization Plan (RaMP) guidance as the default recommended approach for securing privileged users, replacing the legacy Enhanced Security Admin Environment (ESAE) approach.

**Learn more:** [Developing a privileged access strategy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/privileged-access-workstations/privileged-access-strategy) · [Enhanced Security Admin Environment (ESAE) retirement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/privileged-access-workstations/esae-retirement)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the following on-premises servers running Windows Server:  
  
- Two domain controllers in an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain  
- Two application servers named Server1 and Server2 that run ASP.NET web apps  
- A VPN server named Served that authenticates by using RADIUS and AD DS  
  
End users use a VPN to access the web apps through the internet.  
  
You need to redesign the user-access solution to increase the security of connections to the web apps. The solution must minimize the attack surface and follow the Zero Trust principles of the Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures (MCRA).  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Publish the web apps by using Azure AD Application Proxy.
Configure the VPN to use Azure AD authentication.
Configure connectors and rules in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
Configure web protection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Azure AD Application Proxy publishes on-premises web applications through an identity-aware access service. It supports Microsoft Entra preauthentication and Conditional Access, can apply MFA, and uses outbound connector connections so no inbound firewall connection to the internal application is required. This limits users to the published applications rather than granting VPN-level network access, reducing attack surface and supporting Zero Trust.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra application proxy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-proxy/overview-what-is-app-proxy) · [Security considerations for Microsoft Entra application proxy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-proxy/application-proxy-security)

You are planning the security requirements for Azure Cosmos DB Core (SQL) API accounts.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that audits every user who accesses data in the Azure Cosmos DB accounts.  
  
Which two configurations should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Send the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) sign-in logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
Send the Azure Cosmos DB logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
Disable local authentication for Azure Cosmos DB.
Enable Microsoft Defender for Cosmos DB.

questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB data-plane diagnostic logs sent to a Log Analytics workspace capture every data operation and include the Microsoft Entra principal ID of the caller. Disabling local authentication prevents shared-key access and requires Microsoft Entra identities, enabling access to be attributed to individual users.

**Learn more:** [CDBDataPlaneRequests — Azure Monitor Logs reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables/cdbdataplanerequests) · [Azure Cosmos DB built-in policy definitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/policy-reference)

You have an Azure subscription and a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
Your company uses several software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications.  
  
To align with the Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) and Microsoft Cybersecurity Reference Architectures (MCRA), you plan to design a solution that provides visibility into user activity across the applications and detects potentially risky behavior in real time.  
  
Which service should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps provides visibility into cloud-app user and administrator activity, detects anomalous or risky behavior using threat detections and behavioral analytics, and supports real-time monitoring and control through session policies.

**Learn more:** [Control cloud apps with policies — Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies) · [Common threat protection policies — Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-threat-protection)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You have a DNS domain named `contoso.com` hosted by a third-party DNS registrar.  
  
Developers use Azure DevOps to deploy web apps to App Service Environments. Whenever a new app is deployed, a CNAME record for that app is registered in `contoso.com`.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that secures the DNS record for every web app. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that when an app is deleted, its CNAME record is also removed.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for App Service detects dangling DNS entries when an App Service website is decommissioned but its custom-domain DNS entry remains at the registrar. This protection applies when the domain is managed by an external DNS registrar, and it identifies the CNAME condition that must be remediated to prevent subdomain takeover. DNS-record deletion itself must be performed through the registrar or deployment-lifecycle automation.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for App Service – benefits and features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-app-service-introduction) · [Prevent dangling DNS entries and avoid subdomain takeover](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/subdomain-takeover)

Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named Domain1.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
Domain1 is synchronized with the tenant by using Microsoft Entra Connect.  
  
You need to monitor Domain1 for privilege-escalation attacks.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity detects, investigates, and responds to identity-based attacks across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. It monitors Active Directory signals and can detect privilege escalation and suspicious role or group membership changes.

You need to assess the current subscription for compliance with NIST 800-53.  
  
What should you do first?

From Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, create an access policy for cloud applications.

From Azure Policy, assign a built-in initiative that has a scope of the subscription.

questions.explanation:
NIST SP 800-53 regulatory compliance is implemented through an Azure Policy built-in initiative. Assigning that initiative to the subscription establishes the scope that Defender for Cloud evaluates and reports against for compliance.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and an Azure subscription. Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are enabled.  
  
The Azure subscription has 50 virtual machines. Each virtual machine runs different applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be automatically blocked until an administrator authorizes it.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

options.text: Azure AD Conditional Access App Control policies
app discovery anomaly detection policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
adaptive application controls in Defender for Cloud

questions.explanation:
Adaptive application controls in Microsoft Defender for Cloud use machine learning to identify known-safe applications and generate application allowlists for virtual machines. The allowlist can mandate that only approved applications run, preventing unapproved software from executing until it is authorized.

**Learn more:** [Azure security baseline for Windows virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/baselines/virtual-machines-windows-virtual-machines-security-baseline) · [Protect virtual machines with Microsoft Defender for Servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-protect-resources)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network and a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You are designing a Zero Trust security strategy.  
  
Which two security controls should you incorporate into the Zero Trust solution? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: Always allow connections from the on-premises network.
Disable passwordless sign-in for sensitive accounts.
Block sign-in attempts from unknown locations.
Block sign-in attempts from noncompliant devices.

questions.explanation:
Zero Trust requires explicit authentication and authorization using all available signals, including location and device health. Conditional access that blocks sign-ins from unknown locations and noncompliant devices enforces those signals; automatically trusting the on-premises network conflicts with Zero Trust, and passwordless sign-in is a security-strengthening authentication approach.

**Learn more:** [What is Zero Trust?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview) · [Zero Trust identity and device access configurations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-identity-device-access-policies-overview)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution for scanning the application code. The solution must satisfy the application development requirements.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
GitHub Advanced Security includes code scanning, which analyzes repository code for potential security vulnerabilities and coding errors using CodeQL or supported third-party tools.\
\
**Learn more:** [Code scanning - GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/code-scanning)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
Your company has devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, or Windows Server.  
  
You are working to improve the devices' security posture.  
  
You plan to use security baselines from the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit.  
  
What should you recommend to compare the baselines with the devices' current configurations?
questions.explanation:
Policy Analyzer is the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit utility for analyzing and comparing Group Policy Objects. It can compare GPOs with current local policy and local registry settings, which enables assessment of a security baseline against an existing device configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit Guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/security-compliance-toolkit-10)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
Your company has devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, or Windows Server.  
  
You are working to improve the devices' security posture.  
  
You plan to use security baselines from the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit.  
  
What should you recommend to compare the baselines with the devices' current configurations?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud custom security standards can be assigned to Azure subscriptions, AWS accounts, and GCP projects. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not supported as a target scope for custom standards.

**Learn more:** [Create custom security standards and recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations) · [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application lifecycle management process based on the Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL).  
  
You need to recommend a security standard for onboarding applications to Azure. The standard will contain recommendations for application design, development, and deployment.  
  
What should be included during the application design phase?

options.text: software decomposition by using Microsoft Visual Studio Enterprise
dynamic application security testing (DAST) by using Veracode
threat modeling by using the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool
static application security testing (SAST) by using SonarQube

questions.explanation:
Microsoft SDL requires threat modeling during the design phase to identify, categorize, assess, and mitigate security threats before they become embedded in the application architecture. The Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool supports this SDL design-analysis activity.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-microsoft-security-development-lifecycle) · [Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/develop/threat-modeling-tool)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has the virtual-machine infrastructure shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810115742-sdr7pjb0.jpg)  
  
The company intends to use Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS) to back up the virtual machines to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend ways to increase backup-strategy resiliency and mitigate attacks such as ransomware.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

options.text: Maintain multiple copies of the virtual machines.
Encrypt the backups by using customer-managed keys (CMKS).

questions.explanation:
MABS uses a security PIN as an additional authentication layer for critical operations such as stopping protection and deleting backup data. Requiring the PIN helps prevent unauthorized disabling or deletion of backups during a ransomware attack.

**Learn more:** [Security features to help protect hybrid backups that use Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-security-feature)

Your company has a hybrid cloud infrastructure in which data and applications are regularly moved between cloud environments. The company’s on-premises network is managed as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809592947-aug2rkr2.jpg)  
  
You are designing security operations to support the hybrid cloud infrastructure. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Govern virtual machines and servers across multiple environments.  
- Enforce standards for all resources across all environments by using Azure Policy.  
  
Which two components should you recommend for the on-premises network? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Arc connects on-premises and multicloud servers to Azure so they can be managed and governed as Azure resources. Azure Policy guest configuration (now Azure Machine Configuration) extends Azure Policy into the operating system of Arc-enabled servers, enabling compliance assessment and enforcement of machine configuration standards across hybrid environments.

**Learn more:** [Cloud-native governance and policy with Azure Arc-enabled servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/cloud-native/governance-policy) · [Azure Machine Configuration documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/machine-configuration/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant synchronized with an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You are designing an Azure DevOps solution that deploys applications to an Azure subscription by using continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines.  
  
You need to recommend the identity types to use as deployment credentials for the service connection. The solution must adhere to DevSecOps best practices from the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: an Azure AD user account that has role assignments in Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
an Azure AD user account that has a password stored in Azure Key Vault

questions.explanation:
Azure deployment service connections should use a secure, scoped workload identity rather than a user account or a stored password. Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework guidance permits user-assigned managed identities with workload identity federation, avoiding managed secrets and enabling least-privilege Azure role assignments.

**Learn more:** [Security considerations for DevOps platforms — Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/security-considerations-overview) · [Use service principals and managed identities in Azure DevOps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/integrate/get-started/authentication/service-principal-managed-identity?view=azure-devops)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and an Azure subscription. Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are enabled.  
  
The Azure subscription includes 50 virtual machines. Every virtual machine runs different applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be blocked automatically until an administrator authorizes the application.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

options.text: app registrations in the Microsoft Entra tenant
OAuth app policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
app protection policies in Microsoft Endpoint Manager
application control policies in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

questions.explanation:
Application control policies enforce an explicit allowlist of software permitted to run. On Windows Server 2019, App Control policies can block unapproved executables and scripts until an administrator updates the policy to authorize them; Defender for Endpoint can centrally support policy monitoring and management.

**Learn more:** [App Control for Business operational guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/operations/appcontrol-operational-guide) · [Allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint scripts with WDAC script enforcement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-wdac-script-enforcement-mde)

Your company uses Azure Pipelines and Azure Repos to implement continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows for deploying applications to Azure.  
  
You are updating the deployment process to align it with the DevSecOps controls guidance in the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures all code changes are submitted by using pull requests before the CI/CD workflow deploys them.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Repos branch policies can protect the deployment branch by requiring pull requests for all changes and rejecting direct pushes. This enforces the pull-request workflow before changes can reach the branch used by CI/CD deployments.

**Learn more:** [Branch policies and settings - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies?view=azure-devops)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is connected to a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com. Sub1 contains 20 virtual networks named Sub1_VNet1 through Sub1_VNet20.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub2 that is connected to a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com. Sub2 contains 20 virtual networks named Sub2_VNet1 through Sub2_VNet20.  
  
You need to deploy an Azure Virtual Network Manager solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Blocks SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet20 and Sub2_VNet20 by using network security groups (NSGs)  
- Blocks SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet1 through Sub1_VNet19 and Sub2_VNet1 through Sub2_VNet19  
- Allows SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet20 and Sub2_VNet20  
- Blocks FTP traffic on all the virtual networks  
- Minimizes administrative effort  
  
What is the minimum number of components required for the deployment?

options.text: • 1 Virtual Network Manager instance• 1 rule collection• 2 NSGs
• 2 Virtual Network Manager instances that each contains:o 1 NSGo 1 rule collection
• 2 Virtual Network Manager instances that each contains:o 2 NSGso 2 rule collections
• 1 Virtual Network Manager instance• 2 rule collections• 2 NSGs

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Network Manager supports cross-tenant connections, allowing one network manager to manage virtual networks in both tenants. Separate rule collections are needed for the VNet1–VNet19 deny policy and the VNet20 exception policy. An `Always Allow` security admin rule for SSH on the VNet20 group takes precedence over, and stops further evaluation by, the NSG SSH-deny rule, while FTP can remain denied. Two NSGs are required for the separate VNet20 resources in the two subscriptions. [Cross-tenant support in Azure Virtual Network Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network-manager/concept-cross-tenant) and [Security admin rules in Azure Virtual Network Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network-manager/concept-security-admins) document the cross-tenant management and rule-evaluation behavior.

**Learn more:** [Cross-tenant support in Azure Virtual Network Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network-manager/concept-cross-tenant) · [Security admin rules in Azure Virtual Network Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network-manager/concept-security-admins)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to implement enterprise-scale landing zones based on the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. The deployment will include one platform landing zone for all shared services and three application landing zones, each of which will host a different Azure application.  
  
You need to recommend which resource to deploy to each landing zone. The solution must meet the Cloud Adoption Framework best-practice recommendations for enterprise-scale landing zones.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Application landing zones host the resources for a single workload or application. Deploying an Azure Key Vault with each application landing zone keeps that workload’s keys, secrets, and certificates isolated within its own lifecycle and security boundary. Azure Firewall, virtual network gateways, and shared DNS are typically centralized platform connectivity services rather than duplicated for each application workload.

**Learn more:** [What is an Azure landing zone?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/) · [Deploy Azure landing zones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/landing-zones/landing-zone-deploy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a hybrid cloud infrastructure.  
  
The company intends to hire several temporary employees over a short time. These employees must access applications and data on the company’s on-premises network.  
  
The company’s security policy prohibits using personal devices to access company data and applications.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives the temporary employee access to company resources. The solution must scale on demand.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Deploy Azure Virtual Desktop, Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access, and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
Redesign the VPN infrastructure by adopting a split tunnel configuration.
Deploy Microsoft Endpoint Manager and Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access.
Migrate the on-premises applications to cloud-based applications.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop delivers centrally managed virtual desktops or applications, allowing temporary workers to access company resources through a controlled remote session instead of directly using personal devices for company data and applications. Pooled multi-session resources and autoscale support scaling capacity as demand changes. Azure AD Conditional Access and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps provide the access and session-security controls needed for this remote-access model.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Virtual Desktop?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/overview) · [Innovation and Azure Virtual Desktop environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/azure-virtual-desktop/innovate)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates on-premises datacenters in Seattle, Chicago, and New York City.  
  
You plan to migrate the on-premises workloads to the East US Azure region.  
  
You need to design a governance solution for the management group hierarchy. The solution must follow Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure principles and ensure that the hierarchy aligns with the Azure landing conceptual architecture.  
  
What should you use to determine which archetype-aligned management groups to create under the landing zones management group?
questions.explanation:
In the Azure landing zones conceptual architecture, the principal workload archetypes are determined by connectivity requirements. The Corp management group is for workloads that need connectivity or hybrid connectivity to the corporate network, while Online is for workloads that need direct internet connectivity or no virtual network. These connectivity needs therefore determine the archetype-aligned management groups beneath Landing zones.

**Learn more:** [Management groups - Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/design-area/resource-org-management-groups)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters that will host web services.  
  
You need to recommend an ingress controller solution to protect the hosted web services.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway integrates with AKS through the Application Gateway Ingress Controller (AGIC) and provides layer 7 ingress. Application Gateway can also use Web Application Firewall (WAF) functionality and TLS policies to protect AKS-hosted web services from common web attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Application Gateway Ingress Controller?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/ingress-controller-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing Azure App Service web apps. The apps have these characteristics:  
  
- The apps use third-party and open-source components.  
- The apps were developed using C#, Python, and Java.  
- The app deployment process is managed by using Azure DevOps.  
- The app source code is stored in GitHub Enterprise Cloud repositories and is protected by using GitHub Advanced Security.  
  
You need to reduce the risk of supply-chain attacks throughout the application lifecycle.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: app governance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

questions.explanation:
Dependabot alerts identify dependencies with known vulnerabilities by comparing a repository’s dependency graph with security advisories. This helps teams remediate vulnerable third-party and open-source components across supported ecosystems before attackers can exploit them.

**Learn more:** [Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependabot-alerts) · [Supply chain security](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/supply-chain-security)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 50 Azure subscriptions.  
  
You need to monitor resources in the subscriptions for compliance with the ISO 27001:2013 standards. The solution must minimize the effort needed to modify the list of policy definitions monitored for the subscriptions.  
  
What are two ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign an initiative to a management group.
Assign a policy to each subscription.
Assign a policy to a management group.
Assign an initiative to each subscription.
Assign a blueprint to each subscription.
Assign a blueprint to a management group.

questions.explanation:
Azure Policy initiatives group related policy definitions into one managed compliance set. Definitions added to an assigned initiative become part of its existing assignments automatically. An initiative may be assigned at a management-group scope, which applies to child subscriptions, or assigned directly to subscriptions. Both approaches therefore allow the ISO 27001:2013 policy set to be changed centrally without revising a separate policy assignment for every definition. Azure Blueprints instead require assignments to be updated to use a newer published version.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Azure Policy initiative definition structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/initiative-definition-structure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 500 users. Each user has a Microsoft 365 E5 license and uses a Windows device.  
  
Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policies apply to Microsoft Exchange Online email and SharePoint Online sites.  
  
You plan to monitor use of third-party generative AI apps by using Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management for AI (DSPM for AI).  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable Microsoft Purview insider risk management for all the users.
Onboard all endpoint devices to Microsoft Purview.
Configure Microsoft Purview data connectors for the generative AI apps.
License all the users for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview requires Windows devices to be onboarded to Microsoft Purview for visibility into sensitive information shared with third-party generative AI sites and for endpoint DLP monitoring or enforcement. Endpoint onboarding is therefore the prerequisite for monitoring this usage with DSPM for AI.

**Learn more:** [Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dspm-for-ai-considerations)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a main office and a branch office.  
  
The main office has 20 on-premises servers running Windows Server that host applications published by using Microsoft Entra application proxy. The main office has 500 on-premises computers running Windows 11. The branch office has 100 on-premises computers running Windows 11.  
  
All computers in the main office are enrolled in Microsoft Intune. The branch office computers are **not** enrolled in Intune.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 ES subscription.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant. A third-party software as a service (SaaS) app is registered in the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to implement Global Secure Access.  
  
You are evaluating compliant network check together with Conditional Access.  
  
Which two scenarios are supported by compliant network check? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: connections to the third-party SaaS app
connections from the branch office computers
Continuous Access Evaluation for Microsoft Exchange Online

questions.explanation:
Global Secure Access compliant network check integrates with Conditional Access to protect sign-in to Microsoft Entra ID-integrated resources, explicitly including Microsoft apps, third-party SaaS apps, and private line-of-business applications, so both the third-party SaaS app and the on-premises applications published through Microsoft Entra application proxy fall within its supported scope, provided users connect through the Global Secure Access client.

**Learn more:** [Enable Compliant Network Check with Conditional Access - Global Secure Access | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant that synchronizes with an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
Your on-premises datacenter contains 100 servers. The servers run Windows Server and are backed up by using Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS).  
  
You are designing a recovery solution for ransomware attacks. The solution adheres to Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
You need to ensure that a compromised administrator account cannot be used to delete the backups.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Azure Backup, configure multi-user authorization by using Resource Guard.
From Microsoft Azure Backup Setup, register MABS with a Recovery Services vault.
From a Recovery Services vault, generate a security PIN for critical operations.
From Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM), create a role assignment for the Backup Contributor role.

questions.explanation:
Azure Backup multi-user authorization uses a Resource Guard to protect critical operations. It requires applicable authorization on the separate Resource Guard, so a backup administrator account without those permissions cannot independently perform protected deletion-related operations.

**Learn more:** [Configure Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard in Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization) · [Security features that protect hybrid backups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-security-feature)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription with Microsoft Defender for Cloud enabled.  
  
You are reviewing the Azure Security Benchmark V3 report shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809479753-7i4jat2y.jpg)  
  
You need to confirm whether Microsoft Defender for Servers is installed on every virtual machine running Windows.  
  
Which compliance control should you evaluate?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint Security covers endpoint detection and response and anti-malware controls for Azure endpoints. Microsoft Defender for Servers, integrated with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, provides EDR capabilities for virtual machines; therefore, its deployment is evaluated under the Endpoint Security control domain.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft cloud security benchmark - Endpoint security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/mcsb-endpoint-security) · [Overview of the Azure Security Benchmark v3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/overview-v3)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data

options.text: DevOps security in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
a branch policy in Azure DevOps

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is applied through Defender for Cloud as security recommendations that are backed by Azure Policy, and Azure Policy (using audit, deny, and DeployIfNotExists/Enforce effects) is what keeps deployed App Service resources compliant with MCSB recommendations — regardless of whether they were deployed via Azure DevOps. "DevOps security in Microsoft Defender for Cloud" (A) assesses pipeline/repository posture such as secret and IaC scanning, and Microsoft Defender for App Service (B) provides runtime threat protection; neither enforces resource-level MCSB compliance. A branch policy (D) governs source control, not Azure resource compliance. So Azure Policy is the recommendation.

**Learn more:** [Manage MCSB in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-mcsb)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Purview.  
  
A Microsoft SharePoint Online site contains a file named File1 with a sensitivity label applied.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to reevaluate Conditional Access policies when a user downloads Filel from the SharePoint site.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Conditional Access app control provides real-time session controls for SharePoint Online. Its authentication-context capability can reevaluate Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies when a sensitive in-session action, such as downloading a sensitivity-labeled file, occurs.

**Learn more:** [Conditional Access app control - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/el-gr/defender-cloud-apps/proxy-intro-aad)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a multicloud environment containing an Azure subscription, an Amazon Web Services (AWS) subscription, and a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) subscription.  
  
You plan to implement Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) using Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to design a solution that provides attack path analysis functionality for each subscription.  
  
What should the solution include?

options.text: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud attack path analysis depends on contextual security data that includes vulnerability information. Enabling agentless scanning supplies vulnerability assessment data for Azure VMs, AWS EC2 instances, and GCP compute instances, supporting attack-path analysis across the connected multicloud environment.

**Learn more:** [Security explorer and attack paths in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-attack-path) · [Agentless machine scanning in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-agentless-data-collection)

    - **Include:** Select apps; Office 365  
  - **Network:**  
    - **Include:** Any network or location  
    - **Exclude:** Selected networks and locations; Site1  
  - **Access controls:**  
    - **Grant:** Require multifactor authentication, Require Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device  
  
You plan to implement the Zero Trust Rapid Modernization Plan (RaMP).  
  
You need to make sure that Policy1 aligns with RaMP best-practice recommendations.  
  
Which setting should you change?

options.text: Exclude: Selected networks and locations; Site1
Grant Require Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device

questions.explanation:
RaMP calls for explicit validation of user and device trust before access on both public and private networks. An exclusion for Site1 prevents the Conditional Access requirements from being evaluated for connections from that location, creating implicit trust based on network location. The Site1 exclusion should be removed or changed so the controls apply there as well.

**Learn more:** [RaMP Checklist—Explicitly validate trust for all access requests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/user-access-productivity-validate-trust) · [Conditional Access: Network assignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-assignment-network)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You have an on-premises datacenter that contains 20 servers running Windows Server. Every server is onboarded to Azure Arc and protected by using Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for identifying the servers that have outdated hardware drivers or firmware.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Change all the servers to Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2.
Add the Microsoft Intune Suite add-on.
Onboard all the servers to Azure Update Manager.
Add Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management add-ons.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management hardware and firmware assessment inventories server hardware, processors, and BIOS, identifies associated weaknesses, and can surface firmware-update recommendations. This assessment is a premium capability available with Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2, not Plan 1.

**Learn more:** [Hardware and firmware assessment - Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-hardware-and-firmware) · [Compare Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management plans and capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/defender-vulnerability-management-capabilities)

questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing 200 virtual machines running Windows Server 2022 that are protected by Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1. You also have an Amazon Web Services (AWS) subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy 100 Windows Server 2022 virtual machines to the AWS subscription.  
  
You need to recommend an agent to deploy on the virtual machines in the AWS subscription. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide consistent workload protection across all cloud platforms.  
- Minimize the number of agents deployed on each virtual machine.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1 focuses on the endpoint detection and response capabilities provided through Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. AWS virtual machines can be directly onboarded for Defender for Servers Plan 1 by using the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent, providing consistent protection with a single agent per server.

**Learn more:** [Connect your non-Azure servers to Microsoft Defender for Cloud with Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/onboard-machines-with-defender-for-endpoint) · [Overview of Defender for Servers in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-servers-overview)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
An external partner has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabnkam.com.  
  
You need to recommend an identity-governance solution for contoso.com that meets these requirements:  
  
- Enables users in contoso.com and fabrikam.com to communicate by using shared Microsoft Teams channels  
- Manages access to shared Teams channels in contoso.com by using groups in fabrikam.com  
- Supports single sign-on (SSO)  
- Minimizes administrative effort  
- Maximizes security  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect is designed for collaborating through shared Microsoft Teams channels across tenants. It lets external users authenticate with their home-tenant identities, supports SSO and cross-tenant access controls, and avoids creating and managing guest accounts in the resource tenant.

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy several containerized, microservice-based applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).  
  
You need to recommend a solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Manages secrets  
- Provides encryption  
- Secures service-to-service communication by using mTLS encryption  
- Minimizes administrative effort  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
The managed Dapr extension for AKS provides APIs for secret management and encryption, secures service-to-service communication with mTLS, and reduces administration by eliminating manual installation and management of the Dapr runtime. [Dapr Extension for AKS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/dapr-overview)

**Learn more:** [Dapr Extension for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Arc-enabled Kubernetes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/dapr-overview) · [Install Dapr Extension for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/dapr)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer has both a Microsoft 365 subscription and an Azure subscription. The customer’s devices run Windows, iOS, Android, or macOS. The Windows devices are deployed both on-premises and in Azure.  
  
You need to design a security solution that assesses whether every device complies with the customer’s compliance rules. What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Endpoint Manager, through its Intune capabilities, provides cross-platform device management and device-compliance policies for Windows, iOS, Android, and macOS. These policies evaluate whether devices meet defined organizational requirements and report their compliance status.

**Learn more:** [Device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/compliance/overview) · [Plan for compliance policies in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a new Azure environment that follows the security best practices in the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. The environment will have one subscription for shared infrastructure components and three distinct subscriptions for applications.  
  
You need to recommend a deployment solution that includes network security groups (NSGs), Azure Firewall, Azure Key Vault, and Azure Bastion. The solution must reduce deployment effort and adhere to Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure security best practices.  
  
What should be included in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
The Azure landing zone accelerator provides an opinionated, deployable implementation of the Azure landing zone reference architecture. It establishes centralized platform services for shared infrastructure and governed application landing zones, helping deploy security and networking controls consistently across subscriptions with less implementation effort.

**Learn more:** [Deploy Azure landing zones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/landing-zones/landing-zone-deploy) · [Security design in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/design-area/security)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an operational model based on the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that concentrates on cloud-centric control areas for protecting resources such as endpoints, databases, files, and storage accounts.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: security baselines in the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark security baselines are standardized, service-specific guidance describing available security capabilities and recommended configurations. They focus on cloud-centric control areas and support protection of Azure workloads, data, and services, including endpoints and storage-related resources.

**Learn more:** [Security baselines for Azure overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/security-baselines-overview) · [Microsoft cloud security benchmark introduction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/introduction)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have several Azure subscriptions, each containing multiple resource groups.  
  
You need to identify the privileged role assignments in every subscription and the related security risks. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: access reviews in Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
access reviews in Microsoft Entra ID Identity Governance
Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM) discovery
the Analytics dashboard in Microsoft Entra Permissions Management

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management is a CIEM solution that centralizes analysis of cloud entitlements and highlights excessive or high-risk permissions and privileged access across cloud environments. Its Analytics dashboard provides this visibility across Azure subscriptions with less manual effort than configuring and operating separate access reviews for each subscription.

**Learn more:** [View analytic information about users in Permissions Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/entra/permissions-management/usage-analytics-users) · [View privileged role assignments in Microsoft Entra Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/entra/permissions-management/product-privileged-role-insights)

The network contains an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You need to ensure that the domain’s built-in Administrator account can be used only for interactive sign-ins to domain controllers.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the User Rights Assignment security policy settings

questions.explanation:
User Rights Assignment settings in a Group Policy Object linked to the domain controllers OU can deny the built-in Administrator account network, batch, service, and Remote Desktop logons while retaining its local interactive logon capability on domain controllers.\

**Learn more:** [Appendix D - Securing Built-In Administrator Accounts in Active Directory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/appendix-d--securing-built-in-administrator-accounts-in-active-directory)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
The company enters into a contract with the United States government.  
  
You need to review the existing subscription for NIST 800-53 compliance.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Azure Policy, assign a built-in initiative that has a scope of the subscription.
From Azure Policy, assign a built-in policy definition that has a scope of the subscription.
From Defender for Cloud, review the Azure security baseline for audit report.
From Defender for Cloud, enable Defender for Cloud plans.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud implements regulatory compliance standards, including NIST SP 800-53, through Azure Policy initiatives. Assigning the applicable built-in initiative to the subscription scopes continuous compliance assessment to that subscription, after which its status can be reviewed in the Regulatory compliance dashboard.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
Users rely on Microsoft Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and OneDrive to share and collaborate.  
  
The company identifies protected health information (PHI) in stored documents and communications.  
  
What should you recommend to prevent PHI from being shared outside the company?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policies can detect PHI through sensitive information types and enforce actions that block content from being shared with people outside the organization. DLP supports the relevant Microsoft 365 locations, including Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams.

**Learn more:** [Data loss prevention and Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-microsoft-teams) · [Help prevent sharing sensitive items via SharePoint and OneDrive with external users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external)
