questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a group named Group1. The subscription has 1,000 Windows devices joined to a Microsoft Entra tenant and managed by Microsoft Intune. All users sign in to the devices using standard user accounts.  
  
You plan to deploy a new app named App1 to the members of Group1. Group1 members must have administrative rights to install new versions of App1.  
  
You need to ensure that Group1 members can install new versions of App1. The solution must adhere to Zero Trust principles.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: Microsoft Local Administrator Password Solution (Microsoft LAPS)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) allows users to remain standard users while granting temporary elevation for IT-approved applications and installers, including application installations. Elevation rules can scope the approval to App1, avoiding permanent local administrator rights and enforcing least privilege in line with Zero Trust.

**Learn more:** [Learn about using Endpoint Privilege Management with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/epm/overview) · [Zero Trust with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/fundamentals/zero-trust-with-microsoft-intune)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises app named App1.  
  
Remote users access App1 by using VPN connections.  
  
You have a third-party software as a service (SaaS) app named App2.  
  
You need to deploy Global Secure Access to manage access to App1 and App2.  
  
What should you use for each app?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Private Access for App2 and Microsoft Entra Internet Access for App1

Microsoft Entra Private Access for App1 and App2

Microsoft Entra Private Access provides Zero Trust access to private corporate resources, including on-premises applications, without requiring a legacy VPN. Microsoft Entra Internet Access secures access to internet and SaaS applications through an identity-based secure web gateway.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 1,000 Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes.  
  
Inbound internet email is scanned for security threats by a third-party cloud service.  
  
You are assessing whether to replace the third-party service with Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

options.text: the accepted domains in Exchange Online

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises server running Windows Server that hosts a Microsoft SQL Server database named DB1.  
  
You plan to migrate DB1 to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend an encrypted Azure database solution that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- Minimizes the risk of malware using elevated privileges to access sensitive data  
- Prevents database administrators from accessing sensitive data  
- Enables pattern matching for server-side database operations  
- Supports Microsoft Azure Attestation  
- Uses hardware-based encryption  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines with virtualization-based security (VBS) enclaves
Azure SQL Database with virtualization-based security (VBS) enclaves
Azure SQL Managed Instance that has Always Encrypted configured
Azure SQL Database with Intel Software Guard Extensions (Intel SGX) enclaves

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database with Intel SGX enclaves supports Always Encrypted with secure enclaves, allowing richer confidential queries such as pattern matching while keeping plaintext unavailable to database administrators who do not hold the encryption keys. Intel SGX is a hardware-based trusted execution environment, and Azure SQL Database uses Microsoft Azure Attestation for SGX enclave attestation. SGX with Azure Attestation provides stronger protection against attacks by actors with operating-system-level administrative access than VBS enclaves; VBS enclaves in Azure SQL Database do not support attestation.

**Learn more:** [Plan for secure enclaves in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/always-encrypted-enclaves-plan?view=azuresql) · [Configure attestation for Always Encrypted using Azure Attestation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/always-encrypted-enclaves-configure-attestation?view=azuresql)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating a ransomware-mitigation strategy.  
  
You conduct a ransomware risk assessment and identify business-critical assets.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for mitigating ransomware threats. The solution must align with Microsoft security best practices.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: Enable firewall logging for auditing, without restricting inbound or outbound traffic.
Use extended patching cycles to reduce the risk of update-related service disruptions.
Implement immutable, offline backups that have restricted access and test restore procedures regularly.
Deploy Privileged Identity Management (PIM) that uses just-in-time (JIT) access and approval workflows.

questions.explanation:
Immutable and offline backups with restricted access protect recovery data from ransomware-driven encryption or deletion; regularly testing restores verifies that critical systems can actually be recovered. Privileged Identity Management reduces the exposure of privileged accounts through just-in-time, time-bound access and approval-controlled activation, limiting the opportunity for attackers to misuse standing administrative privileges.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for ransomware attacks with a backup and recovery plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/ransomware/protect-against-ransomware-phase1) · [Plan a Privileged Identity Management deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan)

questions.question:
Your company is building a new Azure App Service web app.  
  
You are assisting with the design to validate the web app's security.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for testing the web app for vulnerabilities such as insecure server configurations, cross-site scripting (XSS), and SQL injection.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Dynamic application security testing (DAST) tests an application while it is operating and can identify insecure server configurations, cross-site scripting (XSS), SQL injection, and other runtime-observable web vulnerabilities.\
\
**Learn more:** [Develop secure applications on Microsoft Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/develop/secure-develop)

A customer has a hybrid-cloud infrastructure that includes a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and an Azure subscription.  
  
All on-premises servers in the perimeter network are blocked from connecting directly to the internet. The customer recently recovered from a ransomware attack and plans to deploy Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
You need to recommend solutions that meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that the security operations team can access the security logs and the operations logs.  
- Ensure that the IT operations team can access only the operations logs, including event logs from the servers in the perimeter network.  
  
Which two solutions should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a custom collector that uses the Log Analytics agent
Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access policies

questions.explanation:
A custom collector that uses the Log Analytics agent can gather event data from perimeter-network servers without requiring each server to connect directly to the internet, and forward the data to the Log Analytics workspace used by Microsoft Sentinel. Resource-based Azure RBAC scopes log access to specific monitored resources, allowing IT operations personnel to view only operational-resource logs while security operations personnel receive broader access. Conditional Access governs authentication and sign-in conditions; it does not grant or restrict access to log data.

**Learn more:** [Manage access to Log Analytics workspaces - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/manage-access) · [Connect computers without internet access by using the Log Analytics gateway in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/gateway)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that meets the security requirements for the virtual machines.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time (JIT) VM access minimizes exposure from open management ports by keeping inbound access locked down and granting authorized access only when needed, for the required ports and a specified duration. It provides controlled, auditable administrative access to virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand just-in-time virtual machine access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview) · [Enable just-in-time access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that meets the security requirements for the virtual machines.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: web content filtering in Defender for Endpoint

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP), specifically Endpoint DLP, can apply rules to onboarded Windows devices based on sensitivity labels and block uploads of matching files to configured restricted cloud-service domains. This directly controls uploads from OneDrive-synchronized files to external websites.

**Learn more:** [Help prevent sharing of sensitive items with unauthorized cloud apps and services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-create-policy-unauthorized-cloud-apps-services) · [Get started with endpoint data loss prevention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-getting-started)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription with Microsoft Defender for Cloud enabled.  
  
You have an Amazon Web Services (AWS) implementation. You plan to extend the Azure security strategy to the AWS implementation, but the solution will **not** use Azure Arc.  
  
Which three services can you use to secure the AWS resources? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access
Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Containers supports AWS container environments through the AWS connector, including agentless protection capabilities. Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can authenticate and authorize access to the AWS Management Console and AWS resources, and Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management can protect sensitive AWS accounts through Entra-AWS integration. Defender for Servers requires Azure Arc for AWS EC2 instances, and Azure Policy extends governance across cloud providers through Azure Arc.

**Learn more:** [Connect AWS accounts to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws) · [Enable Defender for Containers in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-containers-enable-plan)

questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are assessing an Azure environment for compliance.  
  
You need to design an Azure Policy implementation that can evaluate compliance without modifying any resources.  
  
Which Azure Policy effect should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy's Deny effect evaluates existing resources against the policy rule and marks non-compliant matches as non-compliant without changing any resource properties; it only prevents new or updated requests that don't match the standard from being created, returning a 403 rather than altering the resource. Modify and Append effects actively add or change resource properties/tags, and Disabled effect skips genuine evaluation (resources default to Compliant), so Deny is the effect that assesses compliance while leaving resources unmodified.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deny effect - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deny) · [Azure Policy definitions disabled effect - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-disabled)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com and use Microsoft Intune. Every user in contoso.com has a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license and a Windows 11 device with the Global Secure Access client deployed.  
  
You plan to deploy the following Microsoft Entra Internet Access configuration:  
  
- Enable a baseline profile.  
- Create a security profile named Profile1 with a priority of 300 that contains one web content filtering policy named WCFPolicy1. Configure WCFPolicy1 as follows:  
  - Set **Action** to **allow**.  
  - Include one rule with a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) destination of `*.adatum.com`.  
- Link Profile1 to a Conditional Access policy named CAPolicy1, apply CAPolicy1 to all users, and grant access unless a user's device is noncompliant.  
  
You need to assess the effect of the planned deployment on traffic to these resources:  
  
- https://www.adatum.com:8433  
- https://www.fabrikam.com  
  
Which two traffic scenarios will occur? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Traffic to https://www.fabrikam.com will be allowed from all the devices.
Traffic to https://www.adatum.com:8433 will be blocked from all the devices.
Traffic to https://www.adatum.com:8433 will be allowed from all the devices.
Traffic to https://www.fabrikam.com will be allowed from compliant devices only.
Traffic to https://www.adatum.com:8433 will be allowed from compliant devices only.
Traffic to https://www.fabrikam.com will be blocked from noncompliant devices only.

questions.explanation:
The Internet Access traffic forwarding profile acquires TCP internet traffic only on ports 80 and 443. Traffic to `www.adatum.com` on TCP port 8433 is therefore not processed by Global Secure Access, so neither the web-content filtering rule nor the linked Conditional Access policy restricts it. HTTPS traffic to `www.fabrikam.com` uses TCP port 443 and is acquired; CAPolicy1 permits that traffic only when the device is compliant.

**Learn more:** [How to manage the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-manage-internet-access-profile) · [Apply Conditional Access policies to Global Secure Access traffic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-target-resource-microsoft-profile)

You need to recommend a solution that detects threats in files after they are uploaded to a blob container.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: sensitive data threat detection in Microsoft Defender for Storage
runtime threat protection in Microsoft Defender for Containers

questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities

options.text: Azure service principals with usernames and passwords
Azure service principals with certificate credentials

questions.explanation:
Azure API Management supports managed identities, and the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark recommends managed identities for Azure services because their credentials are platform-managed, protected, and rotated automatically. This eliminates the need to store long-lived passwords, certificates, or client secrets in application configuration or code.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark - Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/mcsb-identity-management) · [Authenticate with managed identity in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-managed-identity-policy)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend creating private endpoints for the web app and the database layer.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure App Service private endpoint secures inbound access to the app only; it is not used for outbound connections from the app. Private access from the web app to Azure Cosmos DB requires App Service virtual network integration, private DNS resolution, and a Cosmos DB private endpoint. Creating private endpoints alone therefore does not provide the required private database connection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure App Service apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-private-endpoint) · [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using Azure Key Vault to store the credentials.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault protects Azure Cosmos DB credentials from being stored in application code or clear-text configuration. Azure App Service can retrieve Key Vault secrets by using a managed identity, restricting secret access to the workload and enabling secure credential use for the database connection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Store and use Azure Cosmos DB credentials with Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/store-credentials-key-vault) · [Use Key Vault references as app settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend deploying Azure Application Gateway with Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway with WAF protects web applications against common HTTP-based exploits and vulnerabilities, primarily at the web application's ingress. It does not secure the Azure App Service-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection with private, explicitly authorized network access. Azure Cosmos DB can be restricted to private endpoints and have public network access disabled to support this Zero Trust requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Application Gateway?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/ag-overview) · [Configure Azure Private Link for an Azure Cosmos DB account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-private-endpoints)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
Solution: You recommend deploying Azure Front Door with Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF protects incoming web application requests at the network edge from common web exploits; it is not a control for the application-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection. Securing that connection under Zero Trust requires private network access and explicit identity-based authorization for the workload.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/afds-overview) · [Secure your Azure Front Door deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/secure-front-door)

You need to ensure that every incoming request to the apps is inspected for threats by using the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Core Rule Set (CRS). The solution must meet these requirements:

You have an on-premises datacenter and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster called AKS1.  
  
You need to limit Internet access to AKS1’s public endpoint. The solution must ensure that AKS1 is accessible only from the public IP addresses associated with the on-premises datacenter.  
  
What should you use?

questions.question:
You have an on-premises datacenter and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster called AKS1.  
  
You need to limit Internet access to AKS1’s public endpoint. The solution must ensure that AKS1 is accessible only from the public IP addresses associated with the on-premises datacenter.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Global Secure Access uses traffic forwarding profiles (Microsoft traffic, Private access, and Internet access) to determine which network traffic is routed through the Global Secure Access client. Because App1 is an internet-hosted SaaS application, you must enable and configure the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile so that traffic destined for App1 is tunneled through the Global Secure Access client rather than going directly to the internet. Conditional Access policies can require the Global Secure Access client or a compliant network as a sign-in condition, but they do not control which traffic is actually forwarded through the client; that forwarding behavior is governed by the traffic forwarding profile configuration.

**Learn more:** [Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles - Global Secure Access | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-traffic-forwarding) · [Tutorial: Enable Internet Access Traffic Forwarding - Global Secure Access | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/tutorial-internet-access-enable-traffic-forwarding)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft Entra tenant configured with Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
  
You are planning to publish a set of internal web applications using a Global Secure Access application.  
  
You need to make sure users can reach these web apps by connecting through the Global Secure Access application.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a Conditional Access policy that grants access from only compliant devices
a forwarding profile that directs all outbound internet traffic through the Microsoft backbone network
a connector group that contains the connectors used to access the web apps and a single endpoint for the internal fully qualified domain names (FQDNs)
an access policy that limits connections based on user groups

questions.explanation:
To publish internal resources through a Global Secure Access (Private Access) Enterprise application, you must configure a private network connector group containing the connectors that can reach the target resources, and then add an application segment that specifies the internal fully qualified domain name (or IP address/range) and port for the web app. This connector group and FQDN endpoint definition is what enables the Global Secure Access client to intercept traffic destined for that FQDN, route it through the service, and have the connector forward it to the internal web app. Without this configuration, there is no mapping between the published app and the internal resource, so no traffic can be routed even if access policies or Conditional Access controls are in place.

**Learn more:** [How to configure per-app access using Global Secure Access applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-per-app-access) · [How to configure Quick Access for Global Secure Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-quick-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
The company has just signed a contract with the United States government.  
  
You need to review the current subscription for NIST 800-53 compliance.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Azure Policy, assign a built-in policy definition that has a scope of the subscription.
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, create an access policy for cloud applications.
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, turn on a security standard.
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, review the secure score recommendations.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud's Regulatory Compliance dashboard evaluates a subscription against industry, regulatory, and benchmark standards, but only against standards that have been assigned to that scope. NIST SP 800-53 is not enabled by default, so to review compliance you must first enable it: navigate to Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance > Manage compliance policies, select the subscription, open Security policies, and toggle the NIST SP 800-53 standard to On. Once enabled, Defender for Cloud maps its continuous assessments to the NIST 800-53 controls and displays compliant/non-compliant status in the Regulatory Compliance dashboard.

**Learn more:** [Regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/update-regulatory-compliance-packages)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network contains an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to evaluate the security and governance of the domains. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Identify configuration issues and administrative vulnerabilities.  
- Minimize effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity includes identity security posture assessments that proactively scan on-premises Active Directory (via its existing sensors) for known misconfigurations, legacy/insecure protocol usage, risky Group Policy settings, and administrative account vulnerabilities. These assessments are surfaced automatically in Microsoft Secure Score with remediation guidance, requiring no extra setup effort beyond the already-deployed sensors — directly meeting the requirement to identify configuration issues and administrative vulnerabilities while minimizing effort. Microsoft Entra ID Protection addresses cloud sign-in/user risk rather than on-prem AD misconfigurations, Microsoft Defender for Servers targets server workload threat protection, and Microsoft Sentinel would require significant custom engineering to achieve equivalent identity governance insights.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Identity security posture assessments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/security-assessment)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1. All users hold a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  
  
Microsoft Intune is used to manage corporate devices.  
  
You are planning to create a Conditional Access policy that will permit access to Site1 only from devices that have been onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to ensure that the devices can be evaluated for compliance by using Intune before the policy is enforced.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access policies that require device compliance rely on Intune compliance policies to evaluate whether a device meets specified criteria—such as being onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and having an acceptable machine risk score—before the device is marked compliant. Only after a compliance policy is created and devices are evaluated against it can a Conditional Access policy use the 'require device to be marked as compliant' grant control to enforce access restrictions to resources like a SharePoint Online site. Windows Autopilot deployment profiles handle device provisioning, not compliance evaluation; app protection and app configuration policies apply to mobile application management scenarios rather than device-level compliance tied to Defender for Endpoint risk signals.

**Learn more:** [Use compliance policies to set rules for devices you manage with Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/protect/device-compliance-get-started) · [Conditional Access: Require compliant devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/require-managed-devices)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain that is synchronized with a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to evaluate the domain to identify potential credential exposure risks. Your solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Provide actionable recommendations to help mitigate the risks.  
- Minimize the amount of administrative effort required.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity continuously monitors on-premises AD DS (and hybrid identity infrastructure) and generates identity security posture assessments, including detection of exposed or leaked credentials (such as plaintext passwords stored in AD attributes) and other identity-related misconfigurations. Each assessment provides prioritized, actionable remediation guidance, and because monitoring is automated and continuous once sensors are deployed, it satisfies the requirement to minimize administrative effort. Microsoft Secure Score aggregates recommendations across products but does not itself perform the deep AD credential exposure analysis; Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps targets cloud/SaaS app usage and shadow IT rather than on-prem AD; and the Microsoft Assessment and Planning (MAP) Toolkit is a legacy inventory tool for migration planning, not security risk assessment.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Identity security posture assessments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/security-assessment) · [Accounts security posture assessment - Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/security-posture-assessments/accounts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 500 on-premises Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that all outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic from the devices is inspected using Microsoft Entra Internet Access. The solution must minimize infrastructure and operational costs.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: Deploy Network Policy Server (NPS) as a RADIUS proxy.
Deploy Network Policy Server (NPS) as a RADIUS server.
Onboard the Global Secure Access client to the devices.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Internet Access (part of Global Secure Access) inspects internet-bound HTTP/HTTPS traffic by having devices route that traffic through the Global Secure Access cloud service. This requires installing/onboarding the Global Secure Access client on the endpoints so traffic can be forwarded per the configured Microsoft traffic forwarding profile, without deploying any additional on-premises infrastructure such as proxy servers or RADIUS/NPS components. Private network connectors instead enable Microsoft Entra Private Access to reach on-premises private applications and are unrelated to inspecting general internet traffic.

**Learn more:** [What is Global Secure Access?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/overview-what-is-global-secure-access) · [Deploy the Global Secure Access client for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-install-windows-client)

questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Azure subscription contains 1,000 virtual machines.  
  
You are planning to enforce a corporate standard requiring that all virtual machines have just-in-time (JIT) VM access enabled.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that will identify which of the virtual machines support JIT VM access.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access is a capability of Microsoft Defender for Cloud (part of Defender for Servers). Defender for Cloud evaluates each VM against JIT eligibility requirements—such as having an associated Network Security Group and being deployed via Azure Resource Manager—and reports, through its recommendations and workload protection dashboard, which VMs are supported for JIT and which are not, letting an organization identify and remediate machines that don't yet meet the standard. Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH connectivity but does not assess or report JIT eligibility; Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is a cloud access security broker for SaaS applications; Microsoft Intune manages devices/endpoints and is unrelated to Azure VM network security posture.

**Learn more:** [Enable Just-in-Time Access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Just-in-time access overview - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview)

You manage a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes 1,000 Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes.  
  
You need to determine which users are vulnerable to phishing attacks.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: spoof intelligence insight in Exchange Online Protection (EOP)
Attack path analysis in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Attack simulation training in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
user activity reports in Microsoft Purview insider risk management

questions.explanation:
Attack simulation training, part of Microsoft Defender for Office 365, lets administrators launch realistic simulated phishing (and other social engineering) attacks against their organization's users. The results show which users clicked malicious links, opened attachments, or submitted credentials, directly identifying which users are susceptible to phishing. This is distinct from spoof intelligence (which analyzes spoofed senders), attack path analysis (which maps exploitable paths to cloud resources), and insider risk management activity reports (which track potentially risky internal behaviors like data leakage, not phishing susceptibility).

**Learn more:** [Get started using Attack simulation training in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/attack-simulation-training-get-started)

questions.domain: Design security solutions for infrastructure

options.text: Perform offline backups to Azure Data Box.
Use Azure Monitor notifications when backup configurations change.
Encrypt backups by using customer-managed keys (CMKs).

questions.explanation:
Azure Backup provides a security feature that requires an additional layer of authentication—a security PIN generated from the Azure portal—before critical operations can be performed, such as disabling soft delete, changing backup policies to reduce retention periods, or deleting backup items and recovery points. This control prevents an attacker (or a compromised account) who has gained control of the subscription during a ransomware attack from being able to delete or tamper with existing backups, thereby ensuring that clean, recoverable backup data remains available for restoration after the attack. This is part of Microsoft's documented ransomware protection guidance for Azure Backup ('Security features to help protect Azure Backup and recovery data from ransomware attacks').

**Learn more:** [Security features to help protect against ransomware attacks - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-security-feature-cloud)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to enforce ISO 27002:2022 standards for new resources deployed to the subscription. The solution must ensure that noncompliant resources are automatically detected.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.explanation:
Azure Policy initiatives let you assign a built-in regulatory compliance initiative (such as the ISO 27001/27002 initiative) at the subscription scope. Once assigned, the initiative automatically evaluates all new and existing resources against the standard's controls and flags any resource that is noncompliant, enforcing the required standard. Azure RBAC only manages who can perform actions on resources and has no role in evaluating configuration compliance against a standard. The regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud only displays compliance status for standards that have already been assigned via Azure Policy initiatives — it is a reporting view, not the mechanism that enforces the standard or triggers detection of noncompliant resources.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy regulatory compliance built-in initiatives](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/samples/iso-27001) · [Overview of the regulatory compliance dashboard - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/regulatory-compliance-dashboard)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft Entra tenant that uses Microsoft Entra ID Governance. For each department, a dedicated catalog and set of access packages have been created to manage access to applications and data resources.  
  
You need to enable team leaders in each department to:  
  
- Add or remove access package assignments for the users in their department.  
- Ensure that the access packages do not appear in each user's My Access portal.  
  
The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the team leaders?
questions.explanation:
The Access Package Assignment Manager role is a built-in, least-privileged Microsoft Entra ID Governance role that allows a delegated user to view, add, and remove assignments for access packages they are authorized to manage, without granting broader catalog or access package management rights. Because assignments made through this role are performed directly by the delegated manager rather than through a user-initiated request, the access packages do not appear as requestable items in the affected users' My Access portal. This satisfies both requirements—managing assignments and keeping the packages hidden from My Access—while granting only the minimum permissions needed, unlike Identity Governance Administrator (too broad), Catalog Owner (manages the catalog and its resources/packages, not just assignments), or Access Package Manager (manages access package configuration/policies rather than solely assignments).

**Learn more:** [View, add, and remove assignments for an access package in entitlement management - Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-assignments) · [Delegation and roles in entitlement management - Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription with 1,000 users and a group named Group1. All users have Windows 11 devices and sign in using their Microsoft Entra accounts. The users do not have administrative rights on their devices.  
  
Members of Group1 remotely assist the users by taking control of their sessions. These remote control sessions run in the security context of the user being assisted.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that will:  
  
- Enable Group1 members to run apps that require administrative rights on the users' devices  
- Ensure the apps run in the context of each signed-in standard user  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (Windows LAPS)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) allows administrators to define elevation rules for specific applications so that standard (non-admin) users can run those apps with elevated administrative rights, while the elevation is scoped to that application and executes in the context of the signed-in standard user rather than requiring a separate administrator account. This matches the requirement that apps run in the context of each signed-in standard user during remote-assistance sessions that operate under the user's own security context. Entra PIM provides just-in-time elevation for Entra/Azure directory roles, entitlement management automates access package requests/approvals for resources, and Windows LAPS manages local administrator account passwords — none of these enable per-app elevation for a standard user's own session.

**Learn more:** [What is Endpoint Privilege Management? - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/protect/epm-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel deployment.  
  
You are developing a solution to ensure that compliance with the MITRE ATT&CK framework is maintained as the framework evolves.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to identify which MITRE ATT&CK techniques are currently NOT addressed by the Microsoft Sentinel deployment.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: the Microsoft Sentinel Health Summary dashboard

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel provides a dedicated MITRE ATT&CK coverage view (Threat management > MITRE ATT&CK) that maps every analytics rule to the tactics and techniques of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, presenting a heat-map/matrix where each cell shows how many active rules map to a given technique. Techniques with no active rules are visibly highlighted as uncovered, letting you search by technique name or ID and drill into related hunting queries to close the gap. This matrix is kept aligned with the current version of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, allowing ongoing compliance tracking as the framework evolves — which is exactly the requirement of identifying techniques not addressed by the deployment.

**Learn more:** [View MITRE ATT&CK coverage in Microsoft Sentinel | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/mitre-coverage) · [View MITRE coverage for your organization from Microsoft Sentinel | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/mitre-coverage?tabs=defender-portal)

You have an Azure subscription that includes five Azure App Service instances hosting public web apps. Each instance is deployed across three Azure regions.  
  
The web apps process sensitive customer data and must be protected against common web exploits and malicious bots.  
  
You need to recommend a security solution that satisfies the following requirements:  
  
- Provides centralized management and updates for protection rules  
- Protects all the web apps without requiring changes to the application code  
- Minimizes costs  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door offers a global entry point with an integrated Web Application Firewall (WAF) that can be configured once as a centralized policy and applied across all backend web apps in every region, using Microsoft-managed rule sets for OWASP threats and bot protection that are updated automatically without needing to alter application code. Because the App Service instances span three regions, using a regional solution like Application Gateway would require deploying and maintaining separate WAF instances per region, increasing cost and management overhead — whereas Front Door's single global WAF policy meets the centralized management and cost-minimization requirements. Azure Firewall (network-layer) and Azure DDoS Protection (volumetric attack mitigation) do not provide web application-layer exploit and bot protection.

**Learn more:** [Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/afds-overview) · [What is Azure Front Door?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-overview)

You have an Azure subscription containing 100 virtual machines. The virtual machines run either Linux or Windows Server.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to discover which of the virtual machines are internet-facing.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud includes asset inventory and attack surface/attack path analysis capabilities that identify internet-facing virtual machines (for example, VMs with public IP addresses or exposed management ports) and generates recommendations such as 'Internet-facing virtual machines should be protected with network security groups.' This makes it the appropriate tool for discovering which VMs are exposed to the internet, unlike Defender for Cloud Apps (SaaS app discovery), Microsoft Sentinel (SIEM/SOAR log analytics), or Azure Network Watcher (network diagnostics without automated internet-exposure classification).

**Learn more:** [Protect your network resources - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/protect-network-resources) · [Identify and remediate attack paths - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/how-to-manage-attack-path)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises application that processes Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and sends the data to Azure. The application includes the following components:  
  
- APIs that receive and send the PII  
- A data ingestion pipeline that stores the PII in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account  
  
A compliance policy requires that all the PII data be encrypted by using encryption keys that are regularly rotated and stored in a central repository.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that adheres to the compliance policy. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which two components should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Choose two. Each correct selection is worth one point.)
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 encrypts data at rest automatically through service-side encryption (SSE). To meet a compliance requirement for centrally stored, regularly rotated encryption keys with minimal administrative effort, you configure SSE to use customer-managed keys, and store and manage those keys in Azure Key Vault, which provides centralized storage, access control, and automated key rotation. TDE, Azure Disk Encryption, Cloud HSM, and Cloud PKI address different services (databases, VM disks, hardware key protection, and certificates respectively) and are not the appropriate mechanisms for encrypting Data Lake Storage Gen2 data at rest.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage encryption for data at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption) · [Configure customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-configure-key-vault)
